literature.headline_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在单一国家截距下,严重发热伴血小板减少综合征的邻居相关分数为 0.149(95% 置信区间 0.120-0.180),在地区特定基线下降至 0.002 以下。 [10.1186/s12879-026-14800-7]
在129例发热伴血小板减少综合征病例中,9例患者被发现同时感染红立克次体,患病率率为7.9%。系统发育分析表明,鉴定出的 7 个序列与 R 紧密聚类。 [10.1038/s41598-025-21505-5]
平均总恢复时间为 16.58 ± 7.86 天。单变量分析表明,出院时间较长与三个变量之间存在显着相关性:血小板下降持续时间延长(r=0.6577,P<0.0001)、症状出现后延迟入院(r=0.7441,P<0.0001)以及心脏/循环系统受累(P=0.0002)。 [10.3389/fcimb.2026.1968174]

papers.source_body_en: Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a tick-borne bunyaviral infection with heterogeneous recovery trajectories and high case fatality. Most prior studies use in-hospital mortality as the primary endpoint; few quantify independent predictors of recovery duration among surviving patients. This study aimed to identify clinical and laboratory factors independently associated with total time from symptom onset to hospital discharge to guide risk stratification and targeted intervention. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of 43 consecutive laboratory-confirmed SFTS survivors discharged from Taizhou Hospital of Zhejiang Province (July 2019–April 2025). Demographics, laboratory values, and organ involvement data were extracted from electronic medical records. The primary outcome was total days from initial symptom onset to meeting standardized discharge criteria. Univariate correlation and group comparisons screened candidate variables; backward stepwise multiple linear regression was applied to identify independent predictors after multicollinearity diagnosis via variance inflation factor (VIF). Model performance was assessed using adjusted coefficient of determination (adjusted R 2 ). All statistical tests were two-sided (α=0.05). Results The mean total recovery duration was 16.58 ± 7.86 days. Univariate analysis demonstrated significant correlations between longer discharge time and three variables: prolonged platelet decline duration (r=0.6577, P<0.0001), delayed hospital admission after symptom onset (r=0.7441, P<0.0001), and presence of cardiac/circulatory involvement (P = 0.0002). Multivariate regression confirmed three independent predictors: platelet decline duration (β=0.63, P = 0.0001), cardiac/circulatory involvement (β=5.33, P = 0.0003), and days from onset to hospitalization (β=1.41, P<0.001). The final model had an adjusted R 2 of 0.7762, explaining 77.62% of variance in recovery time; all included variables had VIF<2.5 without severe multicollinearity. Dynamic monitoring of platelet counts and cardiovascular biomarkers enables risk stratification. papers.full_text: Abstract Background Endemic–epidemic time-series models partition surveillance counts into endemic, within-area and neighbor-associated components; for directly transmitted diseases a large neighbor-associated component is often read as evidence of geographic spread. Scrub typhus, Japanese spotted fever and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome are acarine-borne zoonoses in which sustained person-to-person transmission does not occur, so they provide a biologically motivated negative-control setting for interpreting short-lag associations between human notifications as transmission between areas. Methods We analyzed weekly notifications of the three infections for the 47 prefectures of Japan, 2013–2025, fitting negative-binomial endemic–epidemic models under five area-baseline specifications, from a single national intercept to prefecture-specific effects. Simulations crossed baseline structure and coupling strength, with identical generating and fitted spatial operators in the principal reference grid; disease-calibrated simulations used row-normalized adjacency for generation and binary adjacency for fitting, matching the empirical specification. Results The neighbor-associated fraction under a single national intercept was 0.235 (approximate 95% interval 0.211–0.259) for Japanese spotted fever, 0.151 (0.132–0.172) for scrub typhus and 0.149 (0.120–0.180) for severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome; under prefecture-specific baselines these fell to below 0.001, 0.063 and 0.002. In simulation with coupling set to zero, spatially smoothed baseline heterogeneity produced mean fractions of 0.083 under the common-intercept estimator in the reference grid and 0.027–0.060 in simulations calibrated to each disease—18–40% as large as the empirical estimates—and four additional zero-coupling mechanisms yielded mean fractions of 0.069–0.112 under the common-intercept estimator. With genuine coupling (true fraction 0.142) the common-intercept estimator returned 0.224 whereas prefecture-specific baselines returned 0.141 when the fitted spatial operator matched the generating one. Conclusions The estimated neighbor-associated fraction changed substantially with the specification of background risk, shared temporal structure and spatial weights; appreciable fractions arose with no between-area coupling, and recovery of genuine coupling depended on alignment between generating and fitted spatial operators. Neighbor-associated fractions should be treated as specification-dependent summaries of statistical dependence, reported across alternative baselines and weights and corroborated with independent data before being interpreted as transmission. papers.full_text: Abstract Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) and Rickettsia monacensis, transmitted by Haemaphysalis longicornis and Ixodes spp. ticks respectively, are endemic to East Asia and can cause overlapping febrile illnesses. Despite their shared ecological niches, co-infections remain poorly characterized. This study investigated the prevalence of R. monacensis co-infection in patients with SFTS in Korea using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and sequencing. Clinical samples were collected from 129 patients with SFTS. One-step reverse-transcription PCR was performed to identify the SFTS virus (SFTSV), and rickettsial nested PCR testing targeted outer membrane protein A (ompA). Phylogenetic analysis was conducted to confirm the evolutionary relationships among the different species. Among the 129 SFTS cases, nine patients with SFTSV were positive for R. monacensis, with a prevalence rate of 7.9%. Phylogenetic tree analysis revealed that the seven sequences identified in the present study clustered closely with R. monacensis. This is the first study wherein 7.9% of patients suspected of having SFTS were also found to be co-infected with R. monacensis based on molecular testing. We believe that these findings highlight the need for the differential diagnosis of tick-borne febrile illnesses and raise awareness of the potential co-infection impacts on disease severity and management. elements_zh.main_results: 在129例发热伴血小板减少综合征病例中,9例患者被发现同时感染红立克次体,患病率率为7.9%。系统发育分析表明,鉴定出的 7 个序列与 R 紧密聚类。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对分子检测的依赖和潜在的假阴性而受到限制,但 7.9% 的 患病率 率是基于对临床样本的直接检测,为研究结果提供了中等可信度。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查韩国严重发热伴血小板减少综合征 (发热伴血小板减少综合征) 患者与红立克次体合并感染的 患病率,因为尽管 SFTSV 和红立克次体具有共同的生态位,但其共同感染的特征仍不清楚。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2024 年至 2026 年间在韩国进行,分析了 129 名诊断为 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的患者的临床样本。重点是确定这些患者中红立克次体的合并感染。
analysis_zh.methods: 采用聚合酶链式反应(PCR)和测序检测SFTSV和红立克次体。对 SFTSV 进行一步逆转录 PCR,对 R. 则采用针对外膜蛋白 A (ompA) 的立克次体巢式 PCR。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在129例发热伴血小板减少综合征病例中,9例患者被发现同时感染红立克次体,患病率率为7.9%。系统发育分析表明,鉴定出的 7 个序列与 R 紧密聚类。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在韩国的 发热伴血小板减少综合征 患者中,与红立克次体合并感染的情况值得注意,这突出表明需要进一步研究此类合并感染的临床意义。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了在 蜱媒 发热性疾病的鉴别 诊断 中考虑合并感染的重要性,并可能为韩国改进 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的诊断和管理策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对分子检测的依赖和潜在的假阴性而受到限制,但 7.9% 的 患病率 率是基于对临床样本的直接检测,为研究结果提供了中等可信度。

The investigation analyzed clinical and laboratory variables associated with total time from initial symptom onset to hospital discharge. Across the cohort, mean recovery duration was 16.58 ± 7.86 days, with a median of 15.00 days (interquartile range, 11 to 21 days). Backward stepwise multiple linear regression determined that three clinical factors independently predicted recovery duration: time from symptom onset to hospital admission, duration of platelet decline, and cardiac or circulatory system involvement. The finalized multivariable regression model demonstrated an adjusted coefficient of determination of 0.7762, indicating that these three variables collectively accounted for 77.62 percent of the variance in recovery time. Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome is an acute bunyavirus infection caused by a phlebovirus first identified in China in 2011, with recognized endemic expansion throughout eastern Asia. The disease carries case fatality rates documented between 6 percent and 30 percent across regional cohorts. Primary clinical manifestations include acute high fever, progressive thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and gastrointestinal symptoms, while severe presentations progress toward multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. There is currently no licensed vaccine or targeted antiviral medication, leaving inpatient care dependent upon supportive interventions. Prior clinical research has primarily concentrated on all-cause in-hospital mortality as a binary primary endpoint, identifying advancing age, coagulopathy, and multiple organ injuries as key prognostic factors for fatal outcomes. However, the study authors noted that few prior investigations have quantified continuous recovery durations among surviving patients, an outcome that directly reflects hospital resource consumption, inpatient bed utilization, and rehabilitation requirements. The single-center retrospective study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Taizhou Hospital of Zhejiang Province affiliated to Wenzhou Medical University under approval number K20251018. The institutional review board waived written informed consent because the research utilized de-identified medical records without direct patient contact. Inclusion criteria required a laboratory-confirmed diagnosis of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome established through viral RNA polymerase chain reaction testing or metagenomic next-generation sequencing, alive discharge status between July 2019 and April 2025, and complete electronic medical records. Among screened records, two individuals were excluded due to missing core laboratory or timeline data, and one patient was excluded due to inpatient death. Disease severity was classified using standard criteria: mild disease presented with fever without organ dysfunction; moderate disease involved thrombocytopenia with mild-to-moderate liver or renal dysfunction; and severe disease featured shock, multi-organ damage, altered mental status, or severe coagulopathy. Discover more Engineering job board Research publication platform Scientific instrument sales Laboratory equipment supplier Biotech startup funding All 43 hospitalized survivors received standardized inpatient management consisting of antiviral therapy with ribavirin or favipiravir alongside supportive measures. These supportive interventions included intravenous immunoglobulin therapy, platelet transfusions, fluid resuscitation protocols, and organ-directed supportive therapies as clinically indicated. The primary study endpoint, defined as total time from symptom onset to hospital discharge, measured calendar days from patient-reported initial symptom onset until standardized discharge criteria were satisfied. These discharge criteria required sustained normothermia with an axillary body temperature below 37.3 degrees Celsius for at least 48 consecutive hours, resolution of major systemic symptoms, and peripheral platelet count recovery reaching at least 100 × 10^9 per liter. The duration of acute hospitalization averaged 11.28 ± 6.00 days, with a median of 10.00 days and an overall range of 3.00 to 32.00 days. The time interval from initial symptom onset to hospital admission averaged 5.30 ± 2.95 days, spanning from 1.00 to 20.00 days. The analyzed survivor cohort had a mean age of 66.42 ± 10.04 years, with a median age of 68.00 years (interquartile range, 60 to 74 years) and an overall range spanning 47.00 to 88.00 years. The demographic composition comprised 29 male patients (67.4 percent) and 14 female patients (32.6 percent). Preexisting chronic underlying conditions were recorded in 16 patients (37.2 percent), while 27 patients (62.8 percent) had no documented chronic comorbidities. Admission laboratory evaluations yielded a mean serum sodium concentration of 133.57 ± 3.78 mmol/L (median 134.10 mmol/L; range 127.00 to 141.80 mmol/L). Mean baseline serum calcium was 1.86 ± 0.23 mmol/L (median 1.88 mmol/L; range 0.96 to 2.18 mmol/L). Across the clinical course, the cohort reached a mean minimum platelet count nadir of 39.70 ± 25.03 × 10^9 per liter, with a median nadir of 31.00 × 10^9 per liter and values extending from 10.00 to 123.00 × 10^9 per liter. Discover more Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Organ involvement was evaluated using prespecified diagnostic thresholds applied to electronic medical records. Cardiac or circulatory system involvement was identified in 12 patients (27.9 percent), defined by new arrhythmia, troponin I exceeding 0.04 ng/mL, creatine kinase-MB exceeding 24 U/L, systolic hypotension below 90 mmHg, or echocardiographic left ventricular ejection fraction below 50 percent. Hepatic injury was documented in 36 patients (83.7 percent), defined as alanine aminotransferase above 80 U/L or total bilirubin above 25 μmol/L. Renal injury occurred in 7 patients (16.3 percent), identified by serum creatinine exceeding 106 μmol/L or blood urea nitrogen exceeding 8.2 mmol/L. Coagulation dysfunction was present in 14 patients (32.6 percent), requiring prothrombin time over 14 seconds or activated partial thromboplastin time over 45 seconds accompanied by clinical bleeding. Respiratory involvement was documented in 14 patients (32.6 percent), and nervous system involvement was recorded in 6 patients (14.0 percent). Cardiac complications were assessed at admission or at any subsequent point during hospitalization. Statistical analyses were executed using SPSS 26.0 software, with all hypothesis tests evaluated as two-sided at an alpha significance threshold of 0.05. Continuous variables were assessed for normal distribution using the Shapiro-Wilk test, and Levene tests verified homogeneity of variance across comparative subgroups. Univariate screening utilized Pearson correlation coefficients for continuous variables and independent-samples t-tests or Welch-corrected t-tests for binary organ complications. Univariate analysis revealed strong positive linear correlations between overall discharge time and both the time elapsed from symptom onset to admission (Pearson r = 0.7441, P < 0.0001) and platelet decline duration (Pearson r = 0.6577, P < 0.0001). Conversely, minimum platelet count exhibited a weaker negative correlation with recovery duration (Pearson r = -0.3644, P = 0.0163). Binary comparisons demonstrated significantly longer recovery times among patients with cardiac involvement (P = 0.0002), renal injury (P = 0.0010), coagulation dysfunction (P = 0.0239), and hepatic injury (P = 0.0252), whereas respiratory, neurological, electrolyte, and comorbidity variables lacked significant associations. Variables demonstrating statistically significant univariate associations with recovery duration were entered into a backward stepwise multiple linear regression model utilizing an entry threshold of 0.05 and an elimination threshold of 0.10. Multicollinearity was evaluated using variance inflation factor diagnostics, with an exclusion threshold established for any variable displaying a variance inflation factor of 3.0 or higher. The final predictive model retained three independent predictors, all maintaining variance inflation factors below 2.5: duration of platelet decline, cardiac or circulatory system involvement, and time from symptom onset to hospital admission. In the final regression equation, platelet decline duration yielded an unstandardized regression coefficient beta of 0.63 (P = 0.0001), cardiac or circulatory involvement demonstrated a beta of 5.33 (P = 0.0003), and days from onset to admission produced a beta of 1.41 (P < 0.001). The complete regression model attained an unadjusted coefficient of determination of 0.7922 and an adjusted R2 of 0.7762, with an overall F-statistic of 46.71 (P < 0.0001). The authors proposed distinct pathophysiological mechanisms to explain how these three independent factors influence clinical recovery trajectories. Severe fever with thrombocytopenia virus directly targets and infects vascular endothelial cells, triggering upregulated expression of adhesion molecules and the extensive release of systemic inflammatory mediators that elevate microthrombosis risk and vascular permeability. Myocardial impairment is driven by direct viral myocardial invasion causing mitochondrial dysfunction, alongside cytokine storm-mediated myocardial contractile suppression mediated by elevated circulating interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-alpha. The resulting systemic hypotension, subclinical heart failure, and microvascular ischemia impair circulatory perfusion and substantially delay physiological convalescence. Simultaneously, viral replication suppresses bone marrow megakaryopoiesis while consuming circulating platelets through microvascular thrombi. Because circulating platelets actively participate in inflammatory signaling, microcirculatory perfusion, and the delivery of bioactive growth factors vital for tissue regeneration, extended platelet depletion impedes organ repair, establishing a bidirectional pathophysiological loop that prolongs inpatient rehabilitation and delays clinical recovery. The investigators highlighted several methodological limitations that necessitate a cautious interpretation of their analytical findings. The study utilized a single-center retrospective design with a sample size restricted to 43 surviving patients, limiting statistical power to identify weaker biomarkers and restricting generalizability across geographic regions with differing demographics and viral transmission intensities. Relying on patient recall for symptom onset timing introduced potential retrospective memory bias, while data completeness depended on variable electronic clinical documentation. Furthermore, key virological and immunological markers—including viral load, serial cytokine measurements, and lymphocyte subpopulation profiling—were not systematically collected. Crucially, the authors emphasized a notable methodological constraint: platelet decline duration was defined as the time until platelet counts recovered to 100 × 10^9 per liter, which was itself an explicit prerequisite criterion for hospital discharge. Consequently, patients with slower platelet recovery inevitably met discharge standards later, a circular dependency that may have artificially inflated the association between platelet decline duration and total recovery time. Admission laboratory evaluations yielded a mean serum sodium concentration of 133.57 ± 3.78 mmol/L (median 134.10 mmol/L; range 127.00 to 141.80 mmol/L). Mean baseline serum calcium was 1.86 ± 0.23 mmol/L (median 1.88 mmol/L; range 0.96 to 2.18 mmol/L). Across the clinical course, the cohort reached a mean minimum platelet count nadir of 39.70 ± 25.03 × 10^9 per liter, with a median nadir of 31.00 × 10^9 per liter and values extending from 10.00 to 123.00 × 10^9 per liter. Cardiac or circulatory system involvement was identified in 12 patients (27.9 percent), defined by new arrhythmia, troponin I exceeding 0.04 ng/mL, creatine kinase-MB exceeding 24 U/L, systolic hypotension below 90 mmHg, or echocardiographic left ventricular ejection fraction below 50 percent. Hepatic injury was documented in 36 patients (83.7 percent), defined as alanine aminotransferase above 80 U/L or total bilirubin above 25 μmol/L. Renal injury occurred in 7 patients (16.3 percent), identified by serum creatinine exceeding 106 μmol/L or blood urea nitrogen exceeding 8.2 mmol/L. Coagulation dysfunction was present in 14 patients (32.6 percent), requiring prothrombin time over 14 seconds or activated partial thromboplastin time over 45 seconds accompanied by clinical bleeding. Respiratory involvement was documented in 14 patients (32.6 percent), and nervous system involvement was recorded in 6 patients (14.0 percent). Cardiac complications were assessed at admission or at any subsequent point during hospitalization. Statistical analyses were executed using SPSS 26.0 software, with all hypothesis tests evaluated as two-sided at an alpha significance threshold of 0.05. Continuous variables were assessed for normal distribution using the Shapiro-Wilk test, and Levene tests verified homogeneity of variance across comparative subgroups. Univariate screening utilized Pearson correlation coefficients for continuous variables and independent-samples t-tests or Welch-corrected t-tests for binary organ complications. Univariate analysis revealed strong positive linear correlations between overall discharge time and both the time elapsed from symptom onset to admission (Pearson r = 0.7441, P < 0.0001) and platelet decline duration (Pearson r = 0.6577, P < 0.0001). Conversely, minimum platelet count exhibited a weaker negative correlation with recovery duration (Pearson r = -0.3644, P = 0.0163). Binary comparisons demonstrated significantly longer recovery times among patients with cardiac involvement (P = 0.0002), renal injury (P = 0.0010), coagulation dysfunction (P = 0.0239), and hepatic injury (P = 0.0252), whereas respiratory, neurological, electrolyte, and comorbidity variables lacked significant associations. Variables demonstrating statistically significant univariate associations with recovery duration were entered into a backward stepwise multiple linear regression model utilizing an entry threshold of 0.05 and an elimination threshold of 0.10. Multicollinearity was evaluated using variance inflation factor diagnostics, with an exclusion threshold established for any variable displaying a variance inflation factor of 3.0 or higher. The final predictive model retained three independent predictors, all maintaining variance inflation factors below 2.5: duration of platelet decline, cardiac or circulatory system involvement, and time from symptom onset to hospital admission. In the final regression equation, platelet decline duration yielded an unstandardized regression coefficient beta of 0.63 (P = 0.0001), cardiac or circulatory involvement demonstrated a beta of 5.33 (P = 0.0003), and days from onset to admission produced a beta of 1.41 (P < 0.001). The complete regression model attained an unadjusted coefficient of determination of 0.7922 and an adjusted R2 of 0.7762, with an overall F-statistic of 46.71 (P < 0.0001). The authors proposed distinct pathophysiological mechanisms to explain how these three independent factors influence clinical recovery trajectories. Severe fever with thrombocytopenia virus directly targets and infects vascular endothelial cells, triggering upregulated expression of adhesion molecules and the extensive release of systemic inflammatory mediators that elevate microthrombosis risk and vascular permeability. Myocardial impairment is driven by direct viral myocardial invasion causing mitochondrial dysfunction, alongside cytokine storm-mediated myocardial contractile suppression mediated by elevated circulating interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-alpha. The resulting systemic hypotension, subclinical heart failure, and microvascular ischemia impair circulatory perfusion and substantially delay physiological convalescence. Simultaneously, viral replication suppresses bone marrow megakaryopoiesis while consuming circulating platelets through microvascular thrombi. Because circulating platelets actively participate in inflammatory signaling, microcirculatory perfusion, and the delivery of bioactive growth factors vital for tissue regeneration, extended platelet depletion impedes organ repair, establishing a bidirectional pathophysiological loop that prolongs inpatient rehabilitation and delays clinical recovery. The investigators highlighted several methodological limitations that necessitate a cautious interpretation of their analytical findings. The study utilized a single-center retrospective design with a sample size restricted to 43 surviving patients, limiting statistical power to identify weaker biomarkers and restricting generalizability across geographic regions with differing demographics and viral transmission intensities. Relying on patient recall for symptom onset timing introduced potential retrospective memory bias, while data completeness depended on variable electronic clinical documentation. Furthermore, key virological and immunological markers—including viral load, serial cytokine measurements, and lymphocyte subpopulation profiling—were not systematically collected. Crucially, the authors emphasized a notable methodological constraint: platelet decline duration was defined as the time until platelet counts recovered to 100 × 10^9 per liter, which was itself an explicit prerequisite criterion for hospital discharge. Consequently, patients with slower platelet recovery inevitably met discharge standards later, a circular dependency that may have artificially inflated the association between platelet decline duration and total recovery time. The investigation, focusing on free-living ticks across Jiangsu Province between 2019 and 2024, examined the spatial distribution, seasonal dynamics, and environmental constraints governing key vector species in an area affected by severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, or SFTS. Utilizing an optimized MaxEnt modeling framework alongside descriptive statistics, the research team found that climatic variables strongly govern where these disease vectors can thrive. Furthermore, future climate projections indicate that areas classified as highly suitable for dominant tick species are set to undergo substantial spatial reorganization over the coming decades. Ticks represent critical vectors of zoonotic pathogens across East Asia, playing a key role in the transmission of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome. Despite the public health importance of these vectors, comprehensive evidence detailing their spatial distribution, seasonal activity, and climate-driven habitat suitability has remained limited, particularly at the provincial scale. To address this knowledge gap, researchers Hongliang Chu, Zhiwei Cheng, Zhiming Wu, Yihan Lu, and Ye Yao analyzed surveillance records of free-living ticks collected throughout Jiangsu Province from 2019 to 2024. The authors coupled field monitoring with an optimized MaxEnt modeling framework to characterize environmental determinants and assess projected climate-driven changes in habitat suitability. Discover more Learn Mandarin Explore History Engineering job board Field surveillance across Jiangsu Province yielded a total of 8,860 ticks, which investigators identified across seven species within three genera. news.content: Researchers in China found a newly identified tick-borne virus in 10.4 percent of 3,163 patients they tested. The virus, called Asian longhorned tick nairovirus (ALTNV), also turned up in ticks collected from 15 provinces. Patients infected with ALTNV alone recovered. Among 38 patients also infected with the virus behind severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), seven died. The tick species that carried ALTNV most often, the Asian longhorned tick, has spread across parts of the United States. The Chinese study tested only patients and ticks in China, so it does not show whether the virus is present in U.S. ticks. Searching for a missing cause The work was led by researchers at the State Key Laboratory of Pathogen and Biosecurity in Beijing, with Xiao-Ai Zhang as first author. They reported it in September 2026 in a letter titled “ A Zoonotic Orthonairovirus from Febrile Patients in China .” Their starting point was a gap in diagnosis. More than 30 percent of patients clinically diagnosed with SFTS test negative for Dabie bandavirus (DBV), the virus that causes the disease. The team screened 3,163 patients with fever and a history of tick exposure . They looked for ALTNV genetic material or IgM antibodies, which the immune system makes early in an infection. Among patients who had tested negative for DBV, 15.1 percent tested positive for ALTNV. ALTNV belongs to the genus Orthonairovirus in the family Nairoviridae . Its proteins share less than 80 percent of their amino acids with other species in that genus. Mild alone, worse with SFTS The researchers described 56 patients with ALTNV alone. Fatigue affected 84 percent of them, and 80 percent had gastrointestinal symptoms. Low platelet counts, known as thrombocytopenia, appeared in 38 percent. Raised levels of the liver enzymes called aminotransferases appeared in 36 percent. All of these patients recovered without lasting effects. In the 38 patients carrying both ALTNV and DBV, coinfection was linked to more severe illness. Respiratory symptoms affected 61 percent of them, compared with 38 percent of patients with DBV alone. Kidney impairment affected 84 percent of the coinfected patients, compared with 66 percent. Seven of them, or 18.4 percent, died. The two viruses circulate in the same areas and share a tick vector. The authors call for better tests to tell these tick-borne viruses apart where SFTS is common. Ticks from 15 provinces The team also tested 47,428 ticks gathered across 15 Chinese provinces. ALTNV genetic material turned up in 1.29 percent of them. The Asian longhorned tick, Haemaphysalis longicornis , carried the virus most often, at 1.75 percent. In laboratory experiments, the species passed ALTNV to mice. Outside Asia, this tick can reduce production in dairy cattle by 25 percent in some regions of New Zealand and Australia, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) noted in 2018. A tick spreading in the U.S. New Jersey was the first U.S. state to report the tick, on a sheep in August 2017, according to the CDC. A single female can reproduce without mating. As a result, hundreds or thousands of ticks can build up on one animal or in one area. Ben Beard, Ph.D., was then deputy director of the CDC’s Division of Vector-Borne Diseases. “The full public health and agricultural impact of this tick discovery and spread is unknown,” Beard said in 2018. By October 2025, the U.S. Department of Agriculture had documented the tick in 21 states, with Kansas the most recent. There, it was found on a dog in Franklin County, according to the Kansas Department of Agriculture and the Kansas Department of Health and Environment ( KDHE ). The ticks have been collected from New York south to Georgia and west to Missouri. They are not competent vectors of the bacterium behind Lyme disease , the USDA’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service ( APHIS ) states. Tick surveillance programs In cattle, the species can transmit Theileria orientalis Ikeda, a parasite responsible for bovine theileriosis. U.S. ticks passed it to cattle in the laboratory, and it has been detected in ticks collected in the field. In 2025, the Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station (CAES) reported the first evidence in the U.S. of a longhorned tick infected with Ehrlichia chaffeensis . This bacterium causes human monocytic ehrlichiosis. Dr. Goudarz Molaei is a research scientist and medical entomologist at the CAES and an adjunct associate professor at the Yale School of Public Health . “A rigorous program in mitigating risks should include expanded tick surveillance programs, strict measures to inspect animals, plants, and other imported materials at ports of entry, accurate and proper identification of exotic ticks and pathogens, effective eradication and prevention measures, and the ability to test exotic ticks for both native and nonnative pathogens,” Molaei said. In 2019, an Asian longhorned tick in Virginia was found to be infected with Bourbon virus, the Kansas agencies noted.
